tool.name: COMEBin-LLMopt
tool.description: an LLM-optimized, faster COMEBin for binning metagenomic contigs
tool.command:
#import re
## torch builds its inductor cache path from the user name, which fails for container uids without a passwd entry. export TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="\$PWD/torchinductor_cache" && mkdir 'outputs' 'bam_files' &&
#set $safename_fasta = re.sub('[^\w\-_\.]', '_', str($assembly_file.element_identifier)) ## Copy, not link: COMEBin writes gene-call caches next to the resolved assembly path. cp '$assembly_file' '${safename_fasta}.fasta' &&
#for $file in $bam_files: #set $safename = re.sub('[^\w\-_\.]', '_', str($file.element_identifier)) ln -s '$file' './bam_files/${safename}.bam' && #end for
comebin-llmopt -a '${safename_fasta}.fasta' -o 'outputs' -p 'bam_files' -t "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-12}" #if str($loss): -l ${loss} #end if -n ${learning} -e ${emb_comebin} -c ${emb_cov} -b ${batch} -m ${max_edges} -L ${min_length} #if str($seed): -s ${seed} #end if ## Training device: an NVIDIA GPU if the job sees one, else the CPU (Galaxy decides by where it runs the job). -d "\$(python -c 'import torch; print("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")' 2>/dev/null || echo cpu)" #if $selection.final_selection == 'checkm2': -S checkm2 -D '$selection.database.fields.path' #else: -S partition #end if
## COMEBin-LLMopt exits 0 without bins when no marker-gene seeds are found; ## create empty outputs in that case. && mkdir -p 'outputs/comebin_res/comebin_res_bins' && touch 'outputs/comebin_res/comebin_res.tsv' #if $cami_output: && ( printf '@Version:0.9.1\n@SampleID:%s\n@@SEQUENCEID\tBINID\n' '${safename_fasta}' && awk -v s='${safename_fasta}' 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"} {print \$1, s"_"\$2}' 'outputs/comebin_res/comebin_res.tsv' && echo ) > 'outputs/cami_binning.tsv' #end if

param.name: bam_files
param.label: Input bam file(s)
param.help: One BAM file per sample with the reads mapped to the assembly.

param.name: loss
param.label: Temperature in loss function
param.help: Leave empty for the automatic choice (COMEBin-LLMopt only): 0.1 if the N50 of the binned contigs is above 10 kb, otherwise 0.15.

param.name: max_edges
param.label: HNSW neighbours retained per contig
param.help: Capped automatically at the number of contigs minus one.

param.name: min_length
param.label: Minimum contig length to bin
param.help: COMEBin-LLMopt only. Shorter contigs stay unbinned. For large assemblies (about 100k contigs) 2500 cuts the run time several-fold.

param.name: final_selection
param.label: Choose the final bins with
param.help: COMEBin-LLMopt only. CheckM2 picks the best bins across all Leiden partitions by CheckM2 completeness and contamination; this gave more high-quality bins in our benchmarks. The marker-score option keeps the single partition with the best marker-gene score, as COMEBin does.
param.option: Marker-gene score of the best partition (-S partition)

validator.message: No CheckM2 databases are installed. Ask the Galaxy administrators to install one, or choose the marker-score selection.

param.name: cami_output
param.label: Also write the bins in CAMI (BioBox) binning format
param.help: For evaluation with AMBER or for CAMI submissions. The sample ID is the assembly name.

param.name: seed
param.label: Random seed
param.help: COMEBin-LLMopt only. Set a seed for reproducible results; leave empty for a random seed.

tool.help:
**What it does**
COMEBin-LLMopt is an LLM-optimized, faster version of COMEBin 1.1.0, improved with the help of an AI coding agent, by iterative modification and testing/benchmarking. COMEBin uses data augmentation to generate multiple views of each contig and learns embeddings of coverage and k-mer features by contrastive learning before clustering them into bins.
**Differences from the COMEBin tool**
- **Faster:** about 2.6–2.8× shorter run time on CPUs (faster loss, training batches, coverage features and dropout), with the same bin quality within seed noise. - **More genomes:** the final bins are chosen with CheckM2 (see below). - **Minimum contig length** (new): bin only contigs above a length, for example 2500 bp for large assemblies. - **Random seed** (new): reproducible runs. - **Temperature:** chosen automatically from the assembly N50 when left empty (COMEBin always uses the value given, 0.15 by default). - **More robust:** small assemblies (HNSW neighbours are capped), assemblies without marker-gene seeds (empty output instead of an error) and CheckM failures. - **Extra outputs:** a contig-to-bin table and, optionally, the CAMI (BioBox) binning format. - **GPU:** training uses an NVIDIA GPU when Galaxy runs the job on one, otherwise the CPU.
**Final bins:** by default CheckM2 chooses the best bins across all Leiden partitions. Alternatively, the partition with the best marker-gene score is kept, as COMEBin does.
**Benchmarks** (32 CPU threads; details and plots at https://github.com/paulzierep/COMEBin-LLMopt):
- **Run time:** CAMI II human gut 33 instead of 85 min, BATS medium 14 instead of 39 min, compared with COMEBin 1.1.0 with the same settings. - **Quality:** on CAMI II human gut (scored with AMBER against the gold standard, seeds 42, 7 and 13), the defaults recover 26–30 genomes > 90 % complete and < 5 % contaminated, against 20–21 with COMEBin's final-bin selection, with an ARI of 0.84–0.85.
The changes are listed at https://github.com/paulzierep/COMEBin-LLMopt/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md.
**Input**
- The assembly file in FASTA format. - The corresponding BAM file(s), one per sample, with reads mapped to the assembly (from any mapper, for example Bowtie2, BWA or minimap2), sorted by coordinate. The coverage is computed from them by the tool.
**Output**
- A collection with one FASTA file per bin. - A two-column table: contig ID and bin. - Optionally the same assignment in CAMI binning format (``@Version:0.9.1``, ``@SampleID``, ``@@SEQUENCEID BINID``; bin IDs are prefixed with the sample ID), for AMBER or a CAMI submission. For several samples, concatenate the files of all samples.
Bins with less than 200 kb of sequence are not reported, so very small assemblies can give empty outputs.
The run time is still high for large assemblies, since this is a machine learning tool.
